text.title: GraphQL API Design Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree mapping observable signals to a rule from content/01-core-rules.xml. The first branches route the protocol choice; the rest are blocking schema-shape gates walked in order. The skip-this-methodology branch is always reachable.

decision-tree.root-question: Is the use case multi-client with nested reads or single-client CRUD?

conclusion.verdict: not GraphQL; this methodology does not apply
use REST; GraphQL overhead not paid back
SKIP — convention overhead exceeds the value on a thin single-aggregate facade
design subgraph SDL, run rover subgraph check before merge
BLOCK — emit a <MutationName>Payload instead of a Boolean or ID
BLOCK — move validation and business-rule failures into userErrors[]
BLOCK — declare the policy as an @auth directive or permission class
BLOCK — wrap the list in Connection/Edge/PageInfo
BLOCK — expose a Relay opaque global ID
APPROVE — design spec ready; run the validator and open the PR
SKIP — preconditions in Applies-If not met

text.example: Need: dashboard with org/user/orders, web+mobile clients. → New GraphQL service. → Design SDL with Relay pagination on orders. → Add OrganizationLoader and OrdersByUserLoader, per-request in context. → permission_classes=[IsOrgMember] on every org-scoped resolver. → QueryDepthLimiter(10) + QueryComplexityExtension(200).

18 types + 12 mutations → not a thin facade → no scalar mutation returns → business failures land in userErrors → @auth declared in SDL → every list is a Connection → relations use opaque IDs → APPROVE.
